disease_label_per_paper: ANCA-positive Bartonella endocarditis with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis
presentation_summary: 55-year-old African American man with alcohol abuse and homelessness presented with one week of lower-extremity swelling and dyspnea on exertion, plus fatigue, lumbar back pain, and 10-lb unintentional weight loss in one month.

Admission exam showed fever 38.8 C, blood pressure 169/82 mmHg, pulse 81/min, respiratory rate 18/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, poor dentition, JVD, systolic and diastolic murmurs, bibasilar crackles, and bilateral pitting edema.

Labs showed WBC 4.0 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 8.6 g/dL, platelets 121 x10^9/L, BUN 42 mg/dL, creatinine 5.51 mg/dL, albumin 1.9 g/dL, BNP 11474 pg/mL, ESR 141 mm/hr, CRP 81.4 mg/L, nephrotic-range proteinuria, hematuria, low C3, RF positivity, c-ANCA positivity, and PR3 antibody >8 U.
Echocardiogram showed severe aortic regurgitation with a 1.7 x 0.3 cm aortic-valve vegetation and a small mitral-valve vegetation; three sets of cultures remained negative.
Bartonella serology was strongly positive; the case mimicked ANCA-associated vasculitis but improved with Bartonella-directed therapy plus short steroid exposure.

quality_warnings: Bartonella serology is confirmatory, not ordinary observation.
